items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 19 at 3:29AM AKST until November 19 at 4:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Winds this strong could make driving difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles. Gusty winds could blow around
unsecured objects. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few power
outages may result.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 19 at 3:11AM AKST until November 21 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 8 inches.
Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Central Brooks Range, primarily Atigun Pass.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Near Atigun Pass periods of falling and
blowing snow could significantly reduce visibility to a half mile
or less at times.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 19 at 3:08AM AKST until November 21 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 5 to 10 inches.

* WHERE...Dalton Highway Summits, South Slopes Of The Central Brooks
Range, and Upper Koyukuk Valley.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The heaviest snowfall is expected along south
facing slopes, especially along the Brooks Range. Areas at lower
elevations, including along the Koyukuk River, are expected to see
lesser snow totals.
items.areas: South Slopes Of The Central Brooks Range; Upper Koyukuk Valley; Dalton Highway Summits
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 19 at 3:02AM AKST until November 19 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 8 inches, with
highest amounts around McGrath.

* WHERE...Upper Kuskokwim Valley.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.
items.instruction:
If you must travel, have a winter survival kit with you. If you get
stranded, stay with your vehicle. Visit 511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1
for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 19 at 2:41AM AKST until November 19 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels of 3 to 5 feet above the normal high tide
expected.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding is possible. In Nome, water
could approach homes in the Belmont Subdivision, portions of the
port area will have standing water, and wave run-up will push
water higher than normal. In Golovin, water will approach beach
property.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 19 at 2:41AM AKST until November 19 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...High Water Levels 2 to 3 feet above the normal high tide
line.

* WHERE...Hooper Bay.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels continue to fall as the storm
weakens. The Thursday high tides are expected to be 3 feet above
normal for the first high tide and 2 feet above normal for the
second high tide. Subsequent high tides are expected to be near
normal.
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 18 at 2:29PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Moderate snow. Additional snowfall amounts of 3 to 6
inches with higher amounts up to around 8 to 12 inches in the
Kobuk Valley and higher and southern slopes of the Brooks Range.

* WHERE...Western Interior north into the Western Brooks Range.

* WHEN...Through Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult at times. Snow could reduce
visibility below one mile at times.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 1:32PM AKST until November 19 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This
includes the city of Seward.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS.
